newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pamplona to resume bull run to show "normality".
newsitem.headline: Pamplona to resume bull run to show "normality".

text.p: Pamplona will resume its world-famous running of the bulls on Sunday night after a one-day suspension in solidarity with a Spanish politician kidnapped and shot by Basque separatist guerrillas.
Organisers halted the festival on Saturday night after learning Basque town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco had been shot in the head and critically wounded. He died on Sunday before dawn.
"We are living in times of mourning and suffering but we cannot feel that ETA has also kidnapped the people's normality," Pamplona mayor Javier Chourrant told a news conference on Sunday.
"The rest of the fiesta will become a serene and responsible clamour from those who defend life above death and the dignity of man over the vileness of the criminals."
After calling of Saturday night's bullfights and the bull run scheduled for Sunday morning, officials met after Blanco died, and decided to resume the festival at 9 p.m. (1700 GMT).

It was the first interruption of the festival -- one of Spanish bullfighting's most cherished institutions -- since 1978, when a local youth was killed during fighting between riot police and Basque nationalist demonstrators.
The festivities this year officially began on July 6 and usually last for nine days.

The guerrilla group ETA kidnapped Blanco on Thursday and threatened to execute him in 48 hours unless the Spanish government agreed to change its policy on rebel prisoners. The government rejected ETA's demands.

When the mayor first announced the suspension on Saturday afternoon, thousands of bullfighting fans who had already taken their seats inside the city's main bullfight ring, reacted with cheers of support. Then, rising to their feet, they chanted "Assassins! Assassins!"
"It's a savage act," one bullfighting fan said of ETA's shooting. Pamplona, which has a large Basque community, lies in the Navarre region, on the eastern border of the Basque country.
The anger turned to violence on Sunday morning when hundreds of youths shouting "Sons of Bitches" and "Murderers" attacked a handful of ETA sympathisers in Pamplona.
The rival groups threw bottles and rocks at each other. Police in riot gear with their faces masked tried to break up the clashes.

When the demonstrators tried to storm the headquarters of ETA's political wing, Herri Batasuna, police opened fire with rubber bullets. They also kicked protesters and used batons to beat them back. A number of people were bleeding and bruised in the clashes, witnesses said.
Most of the youths involved in the violence were dressed in the traditional fiesta white costume with red headbands and sashes.
The annual fiesta in Pamplona draws tens of thousands of bullfighting fans and tourists from across Spain and from around the world.
